answer: A registry can resist sybils by requiring each agent to stake a refundable bond that is slashed on proven misbehavior, with the bond size growing with the agent's claimed tier — like an atlas mapping every identity to one verifiable stake. Newcomers start at the foot of the summit ladder: they earn trust only through a comet trail of completed, attested work, and one wallet can hold only one bonded identity because the stake is locked to a single hardware-backed key. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds plus months of honest work, while one honest agent pays once.
